thread:
mike: quick heads-up — CI perf job flagged a new tail-latency regression on paged-attn after the kernel probe change rolled yesterday. p99 is ~18% higher on long-context workloads. anyone else seeing this?
anya: saw it in the nightly traces too. interestingly GPU free memory variance spiked and allocator churn went up. KV-cache churn jumped.
kevin: attaching the short profile snippet i pulled from /tmp/perf-run.log — look at the workspace_allocs and kernel_fallback counts.
kevin: ```
2026-03-17 03:12:02 INFO kernel_selector: chosen=matmul_fused_v2 fallback=matmul_scalar count=3245
2026-03-17 03:12:02 INFO workspace: allocs=11842 frees=11601 peak_bytes=11.3GB
2026-03-17 03:12:02 INFO kv_cache: hit_rate=0.86 prev=0.94
```
olga: the change that probes matmul_fused_v2 added an aggressive workspace reservation for larger blocks. that reduces per-call kernel overhead but increases fragmentation for mixed sequence lengths.
mike: so we traded steady latency for lower average token cost in some traces, but when block reuse is high we get fragmentation -> OOMs/evictions -> more fallback kernels -> tail spikes.
sre-bot: alert: vm-rt-12 saw 3x evictions in the last 2 hours; rolling restart advised if regression persists.
anya: hypothesis: batching/backpressure interacts with the allocator watermark. When a large request triggers a reservation, smaller concurrent batches get squeezed into stale small-block pools causing cross-pool fragmentation.
kevin: experiment idea: two quick switches — 1) revert aggressive probe (fast) 2) introduce a soft_limit for workspace reservations that prefers reusing same-size pools (medium). run both in canary.
olga: added an AB test matrix in the PR: kernel_probe=off / probe_soft_limit=0.7 / keep_reserve_per_stream=true. also logging KV eviction reason codes.
mike: can we measure the effect on KV hit rate and p99 before full rollout? put a short perf harness with these metrics: p50,p95,p99, kv_hit_rate, workspace_peak, kernel_fallback_count.
kevin: running harness now on canary-3, will post numbers. command i used: `scripts/run_perf_harness --suite=paged-attn-long --runs=200 --collect=kv,ws,kern`
deploy-bot: deploy started for canary-3 (rev: r8f3b1) — expected ~10min. :rocket:
kevin: quick results from canary-3 (probe off): p99 down 16% vs prod, kv_hit_rate back to 0.93, workspace_peak -1.2GB, kernel_fallback_count -78%.
anya: nice. looks like probe change was the primary culprit. but we still see occasional spike when mixed sequence lengths >8 in same batch. need improved batch hedging.
mike: follow-ups: (a) add conservative probe default (off) in runtime 0.9.2, (b) implement soft_limit reuse policy for blockpool, (c) add tracing tag to requests so we can correlate sequence-length-mix to block evictions. i'll open tasks.
olga: drafting runtime change PR and a short blurb for release notes explaining the probe tradeoffs.
sre-bot: note: rolling back can be automated if evictions > threshold for 15m. i can wire threshold into release pipeline.
mike: thanks all. nice find — good to keep kernel probing optional until blockpool tuning lands. :thumbsup:
